texts.preamble: M.Sreekumar vs The Commissioner on 20 July, 2015 Author: M.Sathyanarayanan Bench: M.Sathyanarayanan In The High Court Of Judicature At Madras Date: 20.07.2015 Coram The Honourable Mr.Justice M.Sathyanarayanan W.P.No.20617 of 2015 M.Sreekumar ... Petitioner Versus 1 The Commissioner The Corporation of Chennai Rippon Buildings Chennai-600 003. 2 The Commissioner Chennai Metropolitan Police Veppery Chennai-600 007. 3 The Inspector F-3 Traffic Police Station Nungambakkam Chennai-600 034. ... Respondents Prayer: This Writ Petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, seek For Petitioner : Mr.S.Arivazhagan For Respondents : Mr.P.V.Selvakumar (For R1) Standing counsel. Mr. Rm.Muthukumar (For R2 and R3) Government Advocate O R D E R
texts.facts: 2. The petitioner claims that he has put up a bunk shop on the 40 feet Road, Mahalingapuram Main Road in front of No.10 Private House Opposite to No.96 Kamdar Nagar Provisions Store Mahalingapuram, Nungambakkam, Chennai-600 034, for the past 16 years and is maintaining the shop in a hygienic manner and is fully complying with the provisions of Food Safety and Standards M.Sreekumar vs The Commissioner on 20 July, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67633602/ 1 Act, 2006 (34 of 2006). 3. The petitioner submitted a representation dated 05.03.2014 praying for necessary permission to continue to run the said shop on the road belonging to Corporation of Chennai and though, it was acknowledged on 15.03.2014, he has not been favoured with any kind of response and hence, came forward to file this writ petition.
texts.arguments: 4. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that the family of the petitioner is solely dependent upon the income earned out of the said business and prays for appropriate orders. 5. Per contra, Mr.P.V.Selvakumar, learned standing counsel who accepts notice on behalf of the 1st respondent submitted that admittedly, the petitioner is an encroacher and he cannot claim as a matter of right to run a bunk shop on a public road.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 4. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that the family of the petitioner is solely dependent upon the income earned out of the said business and prays for appropriate orders. 5. Per contra, Mr.P.V.Selvakumar, learned standing counsel who accepts notice on behalf of the 1st respondent submitted that admittedly, the petitioner is an encroacher and he cannot claim as a matter of right to run a bunk shop on a public road.
